a life taken.text: Behind many hauntings lies a plain murder: a stranger killed for gain or out of a grudge, then hidden and left to wait. In Chanderi [a half-burnt book reveals that the spirit called Stree was a murdered courtesan|2018-stree]. Fred Krueger [was burned alive by the parents of Elm Street|1984-a-nightmare-on-elm-street] and now hunts their children, while at the closed orphanage Laura's long search for Simón leads her to [the fate of the orphans she once knew|2007-the-orphanage]. The wrong is especially strong in South Asian films, where more than a third carry it.

abandonment and rejection.text: Some wounds are made by absence: a wife sent away, a sister abandoned, a friend who walked off when it mattered. As armies sweep through his village, [the potter Genjūrō sends Miyagi and their small son back to shore|1953-ugetsu] and sails on toward a noblewoman's mansion. In a remote cabin [Mia tries to quit heroin under the eye of her estranged brother David|2013-evil-dead], and on the express to Busan [the workaholic Seok-woo is taking his daughter Su-an to her mother|2016-train-to-busan]. Almost every film that carries this wrong was made in 2000 or later.

an accident and its guilt.text: An unintended death leaves a ghost of its own, made of guilt and of everything left unsaid. After their young daughter Christine drowns, [John Baxter keeps glimpsing a small figure in a red coat in Venice|1973-don-t-look-now]. In Shutter [Tun keeps Jane in the car as they leave the girl they hit lying on the road|2004-shutter], and pale faces soon surface in his photographs, while a spoon stirring in a teacup makes [Chris confess the night his mother died|2017-get-out]. The record holds none of these films before 1960.

bargains with dark powers.text: Some families owe everything to a deal struck with something that should never have been bargained with, for wealth, a child or power, with the bill left for later generations. The Le Domas fortune in Ready or Not [came from a great-grandfather's deal with a mysterious Le Bail|2019-ready-or-not]. In rural Indonesia [a fertility cult answered barren women's prayers at the price of the last child|2017-satan-s-slaves], and in Tumbbad [Vinayak comes home hungry for the treasure of a forgotten god|2018-tumbbad]. After a quiet half century the wrong has returned, with six of its fifteen films made since 2015.

broken trust.text: Horror often begins where a promise breaks: a lie told, a friend betrayed, a secret kept too long inside a family. Deep in the Appalachians, once the tunnel collapses, [Juno admits she has led her friends into an unmapped cave|2005-the-descent]. In Audition [a widower lets a friend stage a fake casting call to find him a new wife|1999-audition], and Ripley learns that [the company man Burke sent the colonists to the eggs for profit|1986-aliens]. Most of its films date from the 1980s on, and more than half are North American.

cruelty and humiliation.text: Public shame leaves a mark that horror is quick to collect on: the cruel prank, the bullying, the laughter of a crowd. In a Stockholm suburb in 1982, [Eli urges Oskar to stand up to the boys who torment him|2008-let-the-right-one-in], and the twelve-year-old who spends his evenings imagining revenge is no longer alone. The same wound lies behind Carrie, Christine and Sleepaway Camp, and six of the nine films that carry it are North American.

cruelty at home.text: Some horror grows inside the home, where a woman is promised away or a father's habits become everyone's debt. In Dakar [Ada is promised to the wealthy Omar while the man she loves sets out across the sea|2019-atlantics], and on her wedding day Omar's bed bursts into flame. In Bad City [Arash works himself ragged under his father's heroin debts|2014-a-girl-walks-home-alone-at-night], while at Bly [a bachelor uncle keeps his orphaned niece and nephew on condition that he is never troubled|1961-the-innocents]. The wrong has sharpened lately, and ten of its twenty-five films are from 2015 on.

disturbing the dead.text: The dead are owed a quiet grave, and horror punishes whoever robs it, builds over it or buries someone the wrong way. In Black Sabbath [a nurse preparing a body for burial slips a valuable ring from the corpse|1963-black-sabbath]. At 112 Ocean Avenue [the dog keeps scratching behind the basement wall|1979-the-amityville-horror] until the Lutzes find a small red room. The wrong belongs mostly to the older films, from Frankenstein and House of Usher to The Texas Chain Saw Massacre, and it has grown rarer since 1980.

exploitation for profit.text: Horror keeps an account book of everything used up for money: land, animals, workers, even death sold as a show. In Dakar [the men who built the gleaming tower go months without pay|2019-atlantics] before they set out across the sea. In Coming Soon [the actress playing Chaba was made to reshoot the hanging until it looked real|2008-coming-soon], and the take in which her sling snapped stayed in the film, while in Nope [a former child star feeds the thing in the valley their horses|2022-nope]. Two thirds of its films come from 2000 onward.

failing to protect.text: Here the wrong is something left undone, a life that could have been saved and was lost to cowardice, passivity or plain neglect. Malcolm Crowe [is shot in his own home by a former patient he failed to help|1999-the-sixth-sense]. A Cincinnati surgeon [has hidden the drink he took before Martin's father died on his table|2017-the-killing-of-a-sacred-deer], and in a rural town [the authorities shrug at a man carrying a demon|2023-when-evil-lurks], so the brothers dump him far from the farm. British and Irish films carry this guilt more often than any other region's, and half of all its films are from 2015 on.

harm done to children.text: The commonest wound behind these films is a child hurt, often by the very adults meant to keep it safe. In The Ring [Samara is an adopted girl shut away by her own parents|2002-the-ring], and the trail ends at a well. Su-mi [finds bruises on her little sister's arms and blames their stepmother|2003-a-tale-of-two-sisters], and Laura's search for Simón leads her to [what became of the orphans she grew up with|2007-the-orphanage]. The record holds none before 1960, yet in films made since 2015 it appears in one of every four.

harming the natural world.text: Nature in horror keeps score: poison a river, cut into a wild place or haul a great animal home in chains, and something comes back for the debt. In Seoul [formaldehyde poured down a drain gives the Han River a creature of its own|2006-the-host]. Carl Denham [brings Kong back in chains to a Broadway stage|1933-king-kong], where the flashbulbs set him loose, and in the Australian outback [Beth Winters films wildlife being hunted for pet food and disappears|1984-razorback]. The wrong reaches from King Kong to Gaia, and five of its fourteen films are from 2015 on.

human sacrifice.text: Some curses begin at an altar, where a child or a young woman was killed to feed a ritual. Behind a vast stone wall [the islanders offer Ann Darrow on an altar as the bride of Kong|1933-king-kong]. In a cave [priests offer a caged boy to the witch Nakita, whose life depends on his blood|1988-veerana], and in the remote village of Harjosari, where children are buried every day, [the curse leads back to three murdered girls|2019-impetigore]. Nine of its thirteen films were made after 2000.

innocents wrongly punished.text: Here the wrong is a verdict: someone blamed, convicted or put to death for what they did not do, or justice simply denied. In the Australian outback [old Jake Cullen stands trial for his grandson's murder because no one believes his story|1984-razorback] of the giant boar that took the boy. In Guatemala [a dictator's overturned conviction leaves protesters trapping his family inside their house|2019-la-llorona], and at night a woman weeps. The record holds only twelve such films, spread thinly from Häxan to Oddity across most of the world.

killing within the family.text: The worst blood in horror is spilled at home: a spouse, a parent, a sibling or a whole household killed by one of their own. As a child [Michael Myers stabbed his sister to death|1978-halloween], and fifteen years later he comes home to Haddonfield in a stolen white mask. A year after [Ronald DeFeo Jr. shot his whole family at 112 Ocean Avenue|1979-the-amityville-horror] the Lutzes move in, and in a Mexican circus [the boy Fénix watches his father cut off his mother's arms|1989-santa-sangre]. Exactly half of its films are North American.

loss that won't heal.text: No one is to blame for this wound, which is why it never closes: a death or a grief that the living, or the dead, cannot let go. In Adelaide [Amelia still cannot face the car crash that killed her husband on the way to the birth|2014-the-babadook]. In House [the aunt who died waiting for her fiancé to come back from the war now devours unmarried girls|1977-house-hausu], and in Mahal [Kamini waited each midnight for a lover who drowned one stormy night|1949-mahal]. It turns up steadily in every era, from Mahal to Talk to Me.

love betrayed.text: Horror has always known what jealousy and a broken vow can raise. In Kwaidan [a poor swordsman comes home to the devoted wife he abandoned for wealth|1964-kwaidan], to a tender welcome that does not last until morning. Öznur [turns to black magic when her cousin Kudret chooses his happy marriage|2014-siccin], and the spell sets jinn upon his wife, while Irena's jealousy [follows Alice through the dark to a basement pool|1942-cat-people]. Latin American films carry this wrong more often than any other region's, in more than a quarter of them.

meddling with life itself.text: Here the wrong is ambition with a scalpel or a test tube, science pushed past the point where it should have stopped. In the House of Pain [Dr. Moreau has been surgically shaping animals into people|1932-island-of-lost-souls], and his beast-men chant his Law in the jungle. In Cambridge activists break into a laboratory and [free a chimpanzee infected with rage|2002-28-days-later], and within seconds the virus leaps to them. The wrong was at its height before 1960, in Frankenstein and The Fly, and more than two in three of its films are North American.

sacred rules broken.text: Some lines are drawn by faith, and horror follows whoever steps over them: a taboo ignored, a ritual done wrong, a god defied. In the hidden realm of the bunian [Si Bongkok swears never to kill another person|1958-sumpah-orang-minyak], and when he breaks the oath his new beauty turns invisible to everyone. In a small Brazilian town [the undertaker Zé do Caixão scorns religion|1964-at-midnight-i-ll-take-your-soul] until a gypsy warns him about midnight. Southeast Asian films carry this wrong more than any others, and not one North American film in the record does.

selfish appetites.text: Sometimes the wrong is done to no one else, only a person's own appetite left to run: lust, hedonism, a taboo hunger or a slow self-destruction. In The Untamed [Ángel mocks gay men in public while secretly sleeping with his wife's brother|2016-the-untamed]. In Annihilation [Lena's husband Kane comes home from the Shimmer gravely ill|2018-annihilation], and she follows his trail into the glimmering zone. The same wound runs through only ten films, from Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde to Hellraiser and The Platform.

sexual violation.text: This is among the cruellest wrongs horror carries, and its ghosts are often the women it was done to. In Chandanghat [a lustful Thakur rapes a young girl who then kills herself|1962-bees-saal-baad], and her spirit is said to have killed him and his son. In a decaying Hong Kong tower block [twin girl ghosts linger in the flat where they died after a rape|2013-rigor-mortis], and in Santa Sangre [Fénix's mother leads a cult devoted to a raped and armless saint|1989-santa-sangre]. The record holds none before 1960, and a quarter of South Asian films carry it.

sins of the ancestors.text: Some guilt is inherited: the crime belongs to a grandfather or a town's founders, and the bill falls due on their children. In Antonio Bay [the six founders wrecked the Elizabeth Dane and built the town on its gold|1980-the-fog], a secret Father Malone finds in his grandfather's hidden diary. On Elm Street [the parents burned Fred Krueger alive|1984-a-nightmare-on-elm-street], and now he hunts their children through their sleep. Half of its eight films come from the 1980s and 90s.

the outsider punished.text: Communities in horror often raise their own monsters by turning on the one who is different. In 1927 [a lynch mob drags the painter Schweick from Room 36 and kills him in the basement|1981-the-beyond] of a New Orleans hotel that stands over a gate of hell. Antonio Bay's founders [wrecked a ship to keep its leprous owner away|1980-the-fog], and on a New England farm [grief and hunger turn the family's suspicion toward Thomasin|2015-the-witch]. Most of its films have come since 1980.

the powerful abuse their power.text: Some horrors start at the top, with officials, companies and churches that lock people away, hide the danger or crush whoever objects. In Seoul [Gang-du's family is quarantined while officials announce a deadly virus|2006-the-host], even as his daughter phones from the sewers. On a remote Welsh island [a cult holds Jennifer for ransom|2018-apostle], its three founders swearing that blood sacrifice made the barren soil fertile. The wrong runs from The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari to Bramayugam, and it was most common in the 1980s and 90s.

war and atrocity.text: Behind some hauntings lies history at its worst: war, massacre, genocide and the violence of empire. In Ugetsu [armies sweep through the potter's village on Lake Biwa|1953-ugetsu], and he sends his wife and son back to shore. In 1944 Francoist Spain [Ofelia's new stepfather tortures and kills to crush the Maquis|2006-pan-s-labyrinth], and in Guatemala [a former dictator convicted of genocide against the Mayan people hears a woman weeping at night|2019-la-llorona]. East Asian films return to it more often than any others.
